subject: Custody logs & temporary KMS carveouts — Novamed pilot triage
messages:
From: Eric Wong <eric.wong@novamed.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Novamed pilot: reduced audit surface for edge devices?

Hannah —

Thanks again for the quick demo yesterday. One follow-up ask from our security team: because our pilot devices operate in constrained networks, we can't ship the full audit stream back in realtime. Is there a supported pattern to temporarily reduce audit granularity (short-term custody logs + aggregated pointers) for pilot/dev devices while still satisfying our compliance checkbox? If not, what would be the minimum design we could sign off on to move the pilot forward?

We need to present something to our CISO by Friday.

Cheers,
Eric
Eric Wong
Head of Security Programs, Novamed

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Novamed pilot: reduced audit surface for edge devices? — triage

Folks — forwarding Novamed's ask. TL;DR: they want a short-lived exception pattern for pilot devices where we keep a minimal custody log (timestamps, request IDs, hash pointers) and batch the full audit stream back to a jurisdictional collector later. Key constraints:

- Must preserve ability to reconstruct events for an on-demand audit (within 30 days).
- Customer will BYOK for keys used in-region; they want assurance about key rotation and availability.
- Pilot timeline: go/no-go to CISO in 4 days.

Asks:
- Product (Marissa) — can we scope a lightweight feature set we can ship as a gated config (pilot toggle) with explicit risk language?
- Infra (Priyom) — feasibility for a temporary escrow/queued-audit pattern + KMS handling for BYOK devices.
- Security (Kimberly) and Ops (Jonas) — compliance gaps and suggested mitigations; what evidence would satisfy a CISO for a pilot?

I'll consolidate and respond to Eric by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-21T12:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Novamed pilot: reduced audit surface for edge devices? — triage

Hannah / team — quick technical read:

- Feasible approach: implement a "custody-lite" mode on the agent that records: request_id, timestamp, operation type, SHA256 of payload, and a compressed event counter. Full payloads are queued locally encrypted and uploaded when connectivity permits.
- KMS/BYOK: devices can encrypt queued payloads with customer-provided public keys. Server-side orchestration needs a mapping table to know which keys to use for which device group.
- Audit reconstruction: we can reconstruct chain-of-events if the queued blobs are retained for 30 days and hashes match. That satisfies forensics needs as long as we provide the hash-to-payload mapping.

Risks / gaps:
- Risk: delayed uploads increase window for tampering — mitigation: require device-local HMAC guarded sequence numbers and periodic signed manifests.
- Risk: lost devices — mitigation: define escrow policy for keys (customer opts into escrow or accepts risk).

Estimate: a scoped pilot path (agent flag + server-side queued ingestion + signed-manifest check) is ~3 sprints (6 weeks) with a focused engineer pair. If we cut scope (no manifest signing, only hashes), we can try a 2-week spike to get evidence artifacts for the CISO.

Happy to pair on a short spike spec.
Jonas
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-21T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Novamed pilot: reduced audit surface for edge devices? — infra notes + attachments

Adding infra constraints and a proposed exception matrix (attached).

Notes:
- KMS model: we can accept customer public keys for at-rest encryption of queued audit blobs. For BYOK rotations, we'll need an API webhook to notify us of revoked keys; otherwise we cannot decrypt queued blobs — policy must call this out.
- Escrow options: short-term (30-day) escrow into our secure cold store (requires signed consent + SLA) OR customer-managed archival (customer pulls).
- Performance: batching window configurable (default 4h) — longer windows reduce uplink but increase forensic gaps.
- Suggested minimal evidence set for CISO sign-off: signed daily manifests (hashes + counts), examples of queued blob metadata, and a one-time proof-of-integrity replay demo.

Action items I volunteered for:
1) Build an "exception-matrix" doc (attached: kms-exception-matrix.xlsx) — maps device group, risk level, and required mitigations.
2) Draft a short custody policy for pilot customers (attached: custody_policy_draft.pdf).
3) Stand up a 2-week spike environment for Novamed with reduced manifests (no full signing) so we can produce evidence for their CISO.

If Security approves, I'll start the spike next Monday and share the test harness.

—Priyom
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Eric Wong <eric.wong@novamed.com>, security@novamed.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-22T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Novamed pilot: reduced audit surface for edge devices? — proposed pilot controls and next steps

Eric — thanks for the patience. Quick summary and proposed next steps attached (custody_policy_draft.pdf) along with our exception matrix (kms-exception-matrix.xlsx). Highlights: 

- Pilot pattern: "custody-lite" mode on device agents. Minimal custody fields (request_id, timestamp, SHA256) retained locally; full payloads queued encrypted with Novamed-provided public keys.
- Evidence package for CISO: 1) signed daily manifest (hashes + counts), 2) sample queued-blob metadata, 3) a 10-minute replay demo showing reconstruction of 48 hours of activity.
- Key handling: BYOK is supported for queued blobs; rotation requires notification to our webhook or we risk having unreadable blobs. We document this in the attached policy.
- Timeline: Priyom proposes a 2-week spike to generate the evidence artifacts (start: next Mon). If CISO requires signing manifests, add another 2 sprints.

Please review the attached draft policy and matrix. Two asks:
1) Eric / Novamed security — can you confirm whether Novamed will: a) provide public keys for pilot devices, and b) accept a documented webhook-based rotation notification process?
2) Novamed — are you ok with a 30-day retention window for queued payloads during the pilot?

If you confirm these two items, we'll start the spike and aim to deliver a reproducible evidence package before your CISO review on Friday.

Thanks —
Hannah
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference

Attachments: custody_policy_draft.pdf (18 KB), kms-exception-matrix.xlsx (34 KB)
